title: What If a Whole Country Slowly Sank? Tuvalu Is Facing It

scenes.text: What if an entire country slowly sank into the sea? One Pacific nation is already planning for it.
Tuvalu's highest point is only about 4.5 meters above sea level, and most of it sits far lower.
Sea level there has climbed about 15 centimeters in 30 years, roughly 1.5 times the global average.
NASA says much of the land and key infrastructure will sit below the average high tide by 2050.
In 2025, about 8,700 Tuvaluans applied for the first 280 places on a new Australian visa, most of those eligible.
Meanwhile, Tuvalu is building new land, more than 10 percent so far. A country trying to outgrow the sea.
